organization_logic.macro_structure: The summary names a first model and a third model and gives each one number. The body builds a topology, flips the ant rule above a crowd threshold, then writes clearance as the minimum of the longest stair, then routes responders on weights that change as stairs empty. Extra exits, languages, and blocked stairs are edits to the same node set. Sensitivity swings speed and stair width. The recommendation mixes those edits with drills.
organization_logic.dominant_pattern: State the textbook rule, break it with a crowd story, replace it, report one number, and call the model reliable.
organization_logic.section_coupling: Section 3.2 fixes the routes that section 3.3 times. Section 3.3's stair clear times become the weights in section 3.4. Section 3.5 reuses both by editing the node set. Section 6 moves the parameters section 3.3 treated as fixed.
organization_logic.argument_quality: Strong on reducing a building to stairs and on refusing to seal a main exit. Weak on calibration: alpha, beta, tau_0 and NC_max are never printed, and the code totals do not match the prose crowd.

main_argument_chains.claim: The shortest clearance is the best choice among the worst stairs, and 417.2 seconds is short enough.
support_steps: The crowd outside a stair does not matter because only one row fits.
Two floors meeting on one stair make the lower floor go first.
The three-floor wing takes longer than the five-floor wing.
The result sits under a stated 15-minute maximum.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Staff the three-floor wing first, since it sets the building time.

main_argument_chains.claim: Responders should take a side door, and the faster route changes with the moment they arrive.
support_steps: Sharing a stair with visitors is rejected because it slows the exit.
A stair's weight is its crossing time plus its remaining clear time.
Route B wins at an early start and route A wins once the stairs are clear.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Pick the route from the arrival time rather than posting one fixed path.
